Alice — thanks for the clear asks. High level summary up front: Redwood will never require escrow of your CA private key. We support two validated patterns for private deployments: (A) Customer-managed root/issuing CA in HSM with CSR-based brokerage and short-lived bridging certs issued by Redwood that carry tenant-scoped SANs; (B) Customer delegates DNS TXT or signed CSR proof and allows Redwood to provision and rotate leaf certs pinned to a customer-provided intermediate (managed by FinBank).

Key operational bullets (ops checklist draft):
- Verify canonical namespace: CloudOps must supply a CSV of canonical FQDNs and the authoritative zone owner for each (e.g., internal.zone.finbank.local / team-internal).
- Prove name ownership: choose one method per zone: (1) DNS TXT token under the zone (preferred for automated renewals), or (2) signed CSR with token signed by customer CA and uploaded to our console (for air-gapped environments).
- HSM integration: if FinBank wants to keep issuing keys in HSM, we can accept a CSR-signer workflow. Redwood creates ephemeral bridge CSRs we send to FinBank HSM signer; FinBank returns signed intermediates with a short TTL and the chain is anchored to your root. No private key leaves your HSM.
- Bridging certs: Redwood will create short-lived (24-72h) bridge certs for runtime SNI termination if you require egress MTLS to external clients; these are created from the signed intermediate you provide.
- Client trust chain: Applications can pin to your root or to the provided intermediate. We recommend app clients validate against your root stored in their trust store (preferred for security teams).
- Audit & logging: we will send every CSR and issuance event to your Splunk/ELK endpoint via secure webhook; retention controls and signed issuance records are configurable.

I attached a one-page ops checklist and a compact playbook PDF. Laura and Marissa, tagging you for ops and compliance input below.

Thanks,

Adding a few practical runbook items from an ops perspective:

1) Zone readiness check (to be run by FinBank CloudOps): ensure the internal DNS server supports TTL <= 60 for TXT records used in token validation, and that there is a documented owner and runbook for rolling those tokens. If TXT tokens aren't available, confirm the HSM CSR signing API endpoint and sample signer payload.

2) OCSP/CRL considerations: for private CAs, CRL distribution points must be reachable by Redwood's provisioning workers. If your CA is air-gapped, use the signed-CSR method and pre-provision a short-lived intermediate signed out-of-band.

3) Fallback routing policy: config in Redwood Console must include a fallback to a Redwood-verified public model variant (no private SANs) for emergency degraded mode — we will not auto-issue public certs for your private FQDNs.

4) Network egress for validation: provisioning workers need one outbound path to your DNS or HSM signer; if your security policy disallows direct outbound, we will use an ephemeral peered provisioning VPC with strict ACLs for the validation window (you must approve peering in advance).
